statement_start: Conditional rank lemma for minimal unsatisfiable positive exact-one systems. Let E be a finite minimal unsatisfiable family of clauses, each on three distinct variables, and let A_E be its incidence matrix over F_3 on the occurring variables. If A_E z = 1 is solvable over F_3, then rank(A_E)=|E| and |E|≤n′−1.
proof: Suppose the rows are dependent: choose coefficients λ_i, not all zero, with Σ_i λ_i r_i=0, and choose j with λ_j≠0. A solution z to A_E z=1 gives Σ_i λ_i=0, hence Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=−λ_j. For any Boolean assignment x satisfying every clause other than j, the dependence gives λ_j(r_j·x)=−Σ_{i≠j}λ_i(r_i·x)=−Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=λ_j in F_3, so r_j·x=1 mod 3. The integer sum of the three Boolean entries in clause j is in {0,1,2,3}; the only value congruent to 1 mod 3 is 1. Thus x also satisfies clause j, contradicting minimal unsatisfiability. Therefore the rows are independent and rank(A_E)=|E|. Every row sums to 3=0 in F_3, so the nonzero all-ones vector on the n′ occurring variables lies in ker(A_E); rank-nullity yields |E|≤n′−1. For the cited four clauses on four variables, each column sum is 3=0 while the RHS sum is 4=1, so A_E z=1 is inconsistent; that example does not refute this conditional lemma.

statement_start: Let E be a finite inclusion-minimal unsatisfiable family of positive exact-one clauses, each on three distinct occurring variables, and let A be its incidence matrix over F_3. If Az=1 is solvable, then rank_F3(A)=|E| and |E|≤n'−1.
proof: Write the rows as r_i. Suppose they are dependent, with coefficients λ_i∈F_3 not all zero, and choose j with λ_j≠0. From Σ_i λ_i r_i=0 and Az=1, dotting with z gives Σ_i λ_i=0, hence Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=−λ_j. Inclusion-minimal unsatisfiability ensures E\{C_j} is satisfiable; choose a Boolean assignment x satisfying all its clauses. Dotting the row dependence with x gives 0=Σ_i λ_i(r_i·x)=λ_j(r_j·x)+Σ_{i≠j}λ_i, since r_i·x=1 for i≠j. Thus λ_j(r_j·x)=−Σ_{i≠j}λ_i=λ_j, so r_j·x=1 in F_3. The integer sum of the three Boolean entries in C_j belongs to {0,1,2,3}; its only value congruent to 1 modulo 3 is 1. Hence x satisfies C_j too, contradicting that E is unsatisfiable. Therefore the rows are independent and rank(A)=|E|. Each row has exactly three 1s, so A times the all-ones vector is zero in F_3. This vector is nonzero because n'≥3, hence nullity(A)≥1. Rank-nullity gives |E|=rank(A)≤n'−1. For the proposed four-clause instance on four variables, each column sum is 3≡0 while the four right-hand sides sum to 4≡1. Summing its equations would imply 0=1, so that instance violates the solvability premise and does not refute this conditional lemma.
